title: Lightweight tail-protector sampler with eBPF spike detector
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce tracer hot-path CPU and allocation overhead while preserving visibility into latency and error tails. Implement a two-stage, low-cost sampling pipeline: (1) an inlined probabilistic early-sampler that emits tiny sketch records for all requests, and (2) a secondary 'tail-protector' component that triggers full-span capture for candidates detected by a lightweight eBPF-based spike detector and the sketches. Goal: cut per-request tracer CPU by >40% at p95 traffic and maintain or improve tail-event capture (p99/p999) relative to baseline.
background: Recent perf regressions in the tracer (observed Jan-Feb 2026) increased allocations on the hot path, driving SLO risk for inference gateways. Existing tail-based sampling experiments are effective but rely on heavier instrumentation inside the hot path or coarse heuristics that miss sudden latency spikes. We need a sampler that minimizes allocations and branch mispredictions on the critical path while still capturing rare but important tail events.
proposed_solution: Introduce an in-process micro-sketch emitter (compact 16B token: trace_id fingerprint + brief timing bucket + 8-bit tag) emitted via a single atomic write to a per-thread ring buffer. A co-located eBPF-based spike detector aggregates kernel-level latency signals and annotates tenant/routing keys. When either the sketch aggregator or eBPF detector raises a heuristic, the ring buffer consumer enqueues a request to a background capture worker that triggers a full span commit to the tracing backend. Key constraints: zero heap allocation on hot path, bounded memory per-thread, backpressure when consumer is saturated, and cryptographic-safe trace_id fingerprints for PII concerns.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype micro-sketch struct and per-thread ring buffer (C++ runtime change) — 4d. 2) Implement zero-alloc hotpath write + minimal API for SDKs — 3d. 3) Build eBPF probe that emits lightweight annotations to the same aggregator via perf ring buffer — 6d. 4) Consumer service that decodes sketches, correlates with eBPF annotations, and schedules full-span capture — 5d. 5) Load test and chaos testing (tail injection) in staging — 4d. 6) Gradual canary rollout to 10% routes then 100% with feature flag — 3d.
milestones: 2026-02-28: eBPF spike detector PoC working in staging
2026-03-12: integration tests + perf bench results uploaded
acceptance_criteria: Hot-path tracer CPU reduced by >=40% at p95 during synthetic load compared to baseline
No heap allocations on hot-path tracer code in production builds (verified by allocator traces)
Tail-event capture (p99, p999) equal or better than current sampling baseline in controlled injections
Backpressure mode drops non-critical sketches gracefully and logs drop metrics
No sensitive identifiers are emitted in micro-sketch (trace_id fingerprinting validated by security)
tech_risks: eBPF probes may not be available in some Private/on-prem kernels — fallback path needed
Ring buffer consumer could become a bottleneck at high burst rates; need autoscaling and graceful shedding
Fingerprinting must be robust to prevent PII leaks — requires crypto review
OSS kernel versions may break eBPF ABI — test matrix required
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated. Start with internal staging routes for non-critical tenants, then 10% canary across low-traffic regions. Monitor: tracer CPU, allocation histograms, sketch drop rate, p99/p999 error capture rate, and end-to-end trace completeness. If sketch drop rate >5% or p99 capture falls below baseline, rollback to previous flag.
